  • Added a license, a code of conduct, contributing guidelines and GitHub issue templates.

Fixes

  • Fixed paths and file names with characters that need URL encoding, such as #.
  • Fixed several case-sensitivity and working-directory issues on Windows and in subprojects.
  • Fixed runs reported as running after the task manager killed them, and jobs reported as failed with --no-wait.
  • Fixed infinite loops with self-referencing aliases in batches files.
  • Fixed hovering over image diffs, dynamic viewers and broken output manifests.
  • Fixed pages crashing when a commit has no reference.

notes.description: The web app got its name, QA-Board, and its documentation website. Bit-accuracy checks, milestones and batches defined in YAML arrived, and the image viewer became a real comparison tool.

highlights.title: Bit-accuracy checks
highlights.description: qa check-bit-accuracy compares a commit's outputs with any reference (branch, tag or commit), with clear reports and file manifests to make it fast. In the web app, a bit-accuracy tab shows which outputs changed.

highlights.title: Milestones
highlights.description: Star important commits or batches as milestones, with a name and a description, and compare any result against them. Milestones can be kept for yourself or shared with the whole project.

highlights.title: Image and text comparison
highlights.description: Images are compared with the reference with synced zoom, pixel diffs, color tooltips, histograms and brightness, contrast and gamma controls. New text, diff and HTML viewers cover the other outputs.

highlights.title: Batches of inputs and configurations
highlights.description: Batches files list the inputs to run on, together with their configurations and database, and support aliases, filters and custom input discovery. Run them with qa batch --batch, on LSF or locally in parallel.

notes.html:
Web app

  • The web app is now called QA-Board.
  • Added search on the commit list, by message, author, branch or batch, and a refresh button.
  • Added favorite projects; projects are sorted by their latest results, and sub-projects show their own avatar, description and color.
  • You can pick any commit, not only a branch, as the commit or the reference to compare with.
  • Visualizations are now defined per commit in the project configuration, and the files each one shows are matched by patterns.
  • The image viewer: press t to toggle between the new and the reference image, and image settings are synced across viewers.
  • Added a configuration tab that shows and diffs all the configuration files and artifacts in a file tree, with syntax highlighting.
  • Two videos play side by side, in sync.
  • The 3D point cloud viewer can color points by intensity, show a mesh, and be moved with the WASD keys.
  • Added an integrations menu on commits, with links to build artifacts and documentation and buttons to trigger external jobs such as Jenkins builds.
  • Added live logs for running jobs, logs for whole batches, and buttons to stop a batch's jobs or delete a batch.
  • Tuning: the exploration plots are saved in the URL, the efficient frontier plot is colored by parameter, the 1D sensitivity plots are split per input and configuration, and you can choose the platform to run on.
  • Results can be exported to a shared folder.
  • Added a page that follows metrics across commits over time.
  • The web app works in Internet Explorer 11.

CLI and project setup

  • Batches files replace the input groups: qa batch --batch (and --batches-file) run over their inputs and configurations, with only/exclude filters and merging of several files.
  • Added --runner local with multiprocessing, and LSF settings now live under runners.lsf in qatools.yaml, with per-batch overrides.
  • Added qa batch --list, --list-inputs and --list-output-dirs to see what a batch would run.
  • Projects can define their own way of finding inputs with iter_inputs, and the kind of inputs with --type.
  • --share (formerly --ci) saves local runs at the central location so they appear in the web app.
  • Configurations can set environment variables for your code with {"ENV": {...}}.
  • Bit-accuracy: qa check-bit-accuracy takes --batch, --reference-platform and ignore patterns (bit_accuracy.ignore), lets you define which files are text or binary, and normalizes line endings on Windows. Added qa check-bit-accuracy-manifest.
  • Added CI helpers (@on_branch(), run_tests()) and GitLab commit statuses, and better support for Jenkins.
  • qa save-artifacts --file saves a list of files instead of the configured artifacts.
  • qa exits with code 1 when runs fail, forwards your code's return codes, and warns when a newer version is available.
  • Improved Windows support: paths, line endings and file names.
  • qa starts much faster.

Server and administration

  • Added daily database backups, with instructions to dump and restore.
  • Old results are garbage-collected once a day.
  • The server is deployed automatically when master changes.
  • Added API endpoints to stop pending runs, update batch metadata and export results.

Documentation

  • Added a documentation website, with an "Edit" button on each page, guides on visualizations and on debugging runs with an IDE.

Notes

  • The CLI was still distributed as the qatools package, configured with qatools.yaml. Versions 0.3.0 to 0.8.0 came out during the year. The --group options became --batch, and --ci became --share.

notes.description: The year QA-Board became a platform: a React web app backed by a database and a REST API, a `qa` command-line tool that wraps any project's code, tuning and automated optimization on the cluster, and the first generic viewers for images, plots and videos.

highlights.title: A new web app, for every project
highlights.description: The server-rendered pages were replaced by a React single-page app, backed by a database and a REST API. It now hosts many projects, each with its commit list, per-commit results, filters and metrics over time.

highlights.title: The qa command-line tool
highlights.description: A small Python package wraps your code so that each run on an input is tracked: qa run for one input, qa batch for groups of inputs on the cluster, and qa init to set up a project with a single YAML file.

highlights.title: Tuning and automated optimization
highlights.description: Parameter sweeps can be started from the web app and run on the cluster, then explored with dedicated plots. An optimizer based on scikit-optimize can also search the parameter space automatically to minimize a loss you define.

highlights.title: Viewers for any output
highlights.description: Output files are shown with generic viewers: Plotly charts, videos, 3D point clouds, and an image viewer with deep zoom, side-by-side comparison and perceptual diffs against the reference.

notes.html:
Web app

  • The commit list can be filtered by branch, committer and date range, including negative filters, and the selected batches and filters are saved in the URL.
  • Added charts that follow the metrics over time, with boxplot summaries, log scale, medians and improvements relative to the reference.
  • Output cards show each run's status (pending, running, failed, crashed), its parameters, its logs with ANSI colors, and a link to the output folder, with a button to copy its Windows path.
  • Added tuning exploration plots: 1D and 2D sensitivity, a parallel coordinates plot of the parameters and the main metrics, and the trade-offs between metrics.
  • Tuning forms support grid and random sampling, arrays and categorical parameters, a label for each experiment, and the platform to run on.
  • Added a viewer switcher on output cards, and the selected tab is saved in the URL.
  • Large components are loaded on demand, for faster page loads.

CLI and project setup

  • Projects are configured with qatools.yaml, and their metrics with a metrics.yaml file (labels, units, targets, whether smaller is better, which ones to show by default).
  • Groups of inputs are listed in YAML files, with globs and lists of globs; qa batch --group runs over them, locally or on LSF.
  • qa batch can cap LSF memory and threads per project, waits for its jobs, and cancels them if it is interrupted.
  • When results already exist, you can choose to skip, re-run, only re-compute the metrics or only sync them (--action-on-existing, also configurable per project).
  • Added qa optimize for automated tuning, with custom loss functions and targets.
  • Added qa check-bit-accuracy to compare a commit's outputs with its reference branch, and qa save-artifacts to save build outputs (with multiple globs).
  • Added qa get to read the CLI's variables, a module entrypoint (python -m qatools), and a sample project.
  • Added sub-projects: a qatools.yaml in a parent folder is inherited, so one repository can host several projects.
  • Runs can be tagged with a label to keep tuning experiments apart, and their parameters are hashed to keep output paths short.

Server and administration

  • Results are stored in a SQL database, PostgreSQL in production, with Alembic migrations.
  • GitLab webhooks keep commits, branches and committers in sync with the repositories.
  • Added a REST API, used by the web app and by the CLI to report runs and their metrics.
  • The server ships as a Docker image, with staging and production environments deployed from CI, behind nginx with HTTPS.
  • Added a cleanup script that deletes old results, configurable per project.
  • Added a Cantaloupe IIIF image server to serve large images efficiently.

Notes

  • The CLI was then distributed as the qatools Python package, configured with qatools.yaml. Version 0.1.0 came out in July 2018 and 0.2.0 in December 2018.
  • QA-Board was used internally at Samsung by a growing number of algorithm teams; it was not open-source yet.

notes.description: Where it all started: a small internal web page to browse and compare the results of an algorithm's CI runs, commit by commit, instead of digging through output folders.

highlights.title: A results browser for CI runs
highlights.description: Each commit that ran in CI got its own page with its metrics, plots, videos and parameters, next to the list of recent commits. Results were read straight from the folders the CI wrote.

highlights.title: Comparing two versions
highlights.description: Two commits could be compared side by side, with metric histograms and a summary table, to see at a glance whether a change improved or regressed the algorithm.

notes.html:
Web app

  • Added a searchable list of commits. Each commit page shows the results on every input: metrics, curves, rendered videos and the parameters used.
  • Added an interactive view of the estimated trajectories, and support for ground truth to compute error metrics such as drift.
  • Commit pages show their git branch, and load faster thanks to caching.

Server and administration

  • The app follows the CI's git-based output folders, and can be served with uWSGI behind nginx.

Notes

  • QA-Board started in September 2017 at Samsung as a small internal Flask server, built to debug the results of a computer-vision (SLAM) pipeline faster. The ideas that shaped the product were already there: one page per commit, a reference to compare against, and rich visualizations of each output.
